mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 20-day return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the median 60-day return is not significantly different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average 20-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS in the same month indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 20-day return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both HOUST and GDPC1 signals weakening housing demand and overall economic activity, which increases recession probability and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the median 60-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly CPI inflation above 3.0% for four consecutive months, combined with a federal funds rate below 2.0%, signals a delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which erodes real equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 60-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.5% for two consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces earnings expectations and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median 60-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).
